node.label: Geoffrey Parker
node.description: A historian of early modern Europe, war and the Spanish monarchy whose work connects military organization with the resources and reach of states. The Army of Flanders and the Spanish Road (1972) began as a Cambridge doctorate under John Elliott, from Elliott’s question of how Spain sustained its army in the Netherlands. The Military Revolution (1988) extended Michael Roberts’s thesis to fortification and the scale of armies, and made it an argument about the rise of the West; it has remained a debate rather than a settled explanation. Global Crisis (2013) connects the political upheavals of the seventeenth century with climatic change across regions.
